Patch 3.0.2: Echoes of Doom was the systems patch heralding the release of the World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King expansion. It introduced the all new 51-point talent systems, the Barber Shop feature, as well as the brand new Achievement system. It also added a new primary profession called Inscription to the game.

Any additional changes to classes prior to Wrath of the Lich King are at the discretion of the Development Team.[http://forums.worldofwarcraft.com/thread.html?topicId=6136435067&pageNo=6&sid=1#101]
Patch 2.4.1 was a minor patch that released on 1 April 2008.
Patch 2.4.3 was a minor patch that released on 15 July 2008.

Patch 3.0.3 was released on November 4, 2008 and contains minor bug fixes and balance adjustments in preparation for the World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King expansion release on November 13, 2008.
Patch 1.3.2 was a Mac-only minor patch that was released on 4 April 2005.

Patch 3.1.0: Secrets of Ulduar is the first major content patch for World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King. Among the highlights of this patch are the opening of the much anticipated Ulduar raid, the Argent Tournament and many notable class changes.
Patch 3.1.1 is a minor bug fix patch released a week after Patch 3.1.0 primarily to fix talent-related issues.
Patch 3.1.1a is intended to be a very minor bugfix patch released a few days after the release of patch 3.1.1 to fix the paladin Exorcism spell toolip.
Patch 3.1.2 is a minor patch dealing with bug fixes and balance changes.
Patch 3.2.0: Call of the Crusade brought a host of new features for World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King and went live on 4 August 2009.
Patch 3.1.3 is a minor patch dealing with bug fixes and balance changes.
Patch 3.2.2 is a content patch that includes a revamp of Onyxia to level 80 content in celebration of World of Warcraft's 5th anniversary.

Patch 3.3.0: Fall of the Lich King is a content patch that included the Icecrown Citadel raid as well as its three 5-player dungeon wings in the Frozen Halls. Patch 3.3 was the last major patch before the release of World of Warcraft: Cataclysm. Undocumented changes can be found at Patch 3.3.0 (undocumented changes).
Patch 3.3.2 opens the last bastion of Icecrown Citadel to the public as well as the next Arena season. Other changes have also been implemented, as well as a cinematic after defeating the Lich King.
Patch 3.3.5 is a minor content patch introducing the Ruby Sanctum raid and cross-game chat using Battle.net. The patch was launched on US servers on 22 June 2010 and on other servers on 30 June 2010.
Patch 3.3.3 is a minor content patch mainly focusing on changes to battlegrounds and some class balance tweaks.
Patch 4.0.1 was the systems patch for World of Warcraft: Cataclysm. This patch did not include Cataclysm features such as the two new races, world changes, quests, and new zones.

Patch 4.1.0: Rise of the Zandalari was the first major content patch for the World of Warcraft: Cataclysm expansion. Among other changes, it featured the return of the Zul'Aman and Zul'Gurub raids as 5-player normal and heroic dungeons.
IMPORTANT NOTE: This is NOT the patch that will implement the world changes, but rather preload them; the world changes will be activated in patch 4.0.3a.

Patch 4.0.6 is a tooltip display fix and class adjustment patch. Hotfixes applied after 4.0.3a updated the actual spells in the game, but not the tooltips used to display them in the client. This patch fixes that, and makes many other balance tweaks to classes, dungeons, items and professions. A very quick bugfix patch was released a few days later in the form of Patch 4.0.6a, which rolls in a number of hotfixes and other bug fixes that could not be made as hotfixes.
Patch 4.0.6a is a bug fix patch, released the same week as patch 4.0.6 in order to fix some bugs that could not be fixed via hotfixes.

Patch 4.2.0: Rage of the Firelands contains the Firelands raid, and is the end of Arena season 9. It has also added a daily quest hub to Hyjal, as well as two new daily quest zones called The Regrowth and the Molten Front. It will continue Thrall's story. It has also introduced the new Dungeon Journal feature.

Patch 4.3.0: Hour of Twilight contains the Dragon Soul Raid and three new Caverns of Time 5-man heroics, and is the end of Arena season 10. This is the largest content release since the opening of Cataclysm.
Patch 5.1.0: Landfall is the first major content patch of Mists of Pandaria, and the beginning of The Pandaria Campaign.

Patch 5.0.4 was the systems patch of World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria, following World of Warcraft: Cataclysm. This patch brought the Theramore's Fall scenario in place of a world event, along with a major overhaul of game mechanics.
Patch 5.0.5a has some fixes and tweaks which couldn't be hotfixed. pl:Patch 5.0.5a
Patch 5.0.5b has some fixes and tweaks which couldn't be hotfixed. pl:Patch 5.0.5b

Patrick "Pat" Nagle is a Senior Game Designer at Blizzard Entertainment. He started working at Blizzard in 1997 and has worked on games from the Warcraft, StarCraft and Diablo franchises. He was one of the original two Quest Designers for the original World of Warcraft, the other being Jeffrey Kaplan. Pagle currently works on Hearthstone, specifically designing new s.

Patch 5.2.0: The Thunder King is the first World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria patch of 2013 that focuses on the return of the Thunder King. It was targeted to be released February 26, but was delayed for March 5. This patch includes a massive new raid dungeon, a multi-faceted new quest hub, Pet Battle improvements, new world bosses, significant class balance changes, brand new pets and mounts, assorted bug fixes, and more. Ten client patches all called "Patch 5.2.0" have been released so far, all to fix minor bugs. See the patch list for more information.

Patch 5.3.0: Escalation is the second non-raid patch of World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria and focuses on the escalating tensions between Garrosh and Vol'jin's Darkspear Rebellion. The patch includes a new world event in the Barrens, the addition of Heroic Scenarios, a brand new Arena and Battleground, new foes to fight in the Brawler's Guild and much more.

Patch 5.4.0: Siege of Orgrimmar is a raid patch of World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria and focuses on the Siege of Orgrimmar from the leaders of the Alliance and the Horde to topple the ruthless warchief, Garrosh Hellscream. The patch includes a new raid, the Siege of Orgrimmar, a new area, the Timeless Isle, and much more. It also features the debut of the Proving Grounds, the Flexible Raid difficulty, and the Connected Realms feature. As another Mists of Pandaria content patch would delay World of Warcraft: Warlords of Draenor, 5.4 is the last content patch of the expansion. Last patch notes update: 2013-09-09
Patch 5.4.1 is the first patch after patch 5.4.0. Last patch notes update: 2013-10-29

Patch 5.4.2 is the second minor patch for patch 5.4.0. It introduced cross-realm mail (for heirlooms) and upgraded the raid browser (not the raid finder) to work cross-realm as well in preparation for Warlords. Last patch notes update: 2013-12-09

Patch 6.0.2 was the systems patch of World of Warcraft: Warlords of Draenor. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on September 9, 2014 and released on October 14, 2014. Last patch notes update: 2014-10-13
Patch 5.4.7 was the first World of Warcraft patch of 2014. It ended Season 14 and set up the start for Season 15 a week later. Last patch notes update: 2014-02-13
Patch 5.4.8 is the fourth minor patch for patch 5.4. Last patch notes update: 2014-05-19

Patch 6.0.3a is what Wowpedia is using to distinguish pre-Warlords Patch 6.0.3 from post-launch content. The next actual client patch was released on December 3, 2014, but Blizzard still called it "Patch 6.0.3", so Wowpedia refers to it as Patch 6.0.3b. Last Blizzard update: November 13, 2014

Patch Day occurs when a new patch is applied to the live game from Blizzard's servers and applied to your client to continue to play World of Warcraft. They are, unlike hotfixes, scheduled to be usually on Tuesdays (weekly maintenance downtime) in North America and on Wednesdays in Europe. Blizzard also likes to use Patch Day for maintenance and upgrades to the forums and Blizzard Battle.net.

Pathaleon the Calculator is the last boss of the Mechanar, which is one of the satellite structures of Tempest Keep. He is the mouthpiece of his demon-crazed master, Kael'thas Sunstrider. He is the head of all the blood elves' devious schemes and has been connected thus far with the massive red crystal at Fallen Sky Ridge in the west of Hellfire Peninsula and a mysterious scheme dubbed "Project at Firewing Point". He is also Kael'thas' personal envoy between the Manaforges in the Netherstorm.

The Path of Glory is an iron-paved road starting northeast of Talador, at a draenei bridge near Frostwolf Overlook and Bladefury's Command, and continuing east to the Gates of Tanaan. There, the path continues through Tanaan Jungle, bisecting the entire zone and leading to the . It's under the control of the Iron Horde. During the Assault on the Dark Portal, the Iron Worldbreaker could be found on the eastern half of the Path. Later, when twisted the landscape, the western part was now split into the Iron Front and the Bleeding Hollow Hunting Grounds, while the eastern half was left unnamed. The area was eventually attacked by Alliance and Horde forces, heading to assault Azuka Bladefury.

The Path of Anguish is a jagged canyon full infernals, imps, and dreadlords, similar to Felspark Ravine further north. It can be found northeast of the Valley of Bones, south of the Path of Glory, and west of the Legion Front. The similarity to the name of the main road, which was dubbed by the orcs, indicates that this has long been an area of defeat for the Horde.

__NOTOC__ The Path of the Titans (called Path of Giants in one source) is a massive, ancient, now-ruined road that runs through the center of Dragonblight. Patient Shui is a pandaren located at the Pinchwhistle Gearworks in Spires of Arak.
Patrolling Draenor is a garrison achievement requiring you to complete 50 garrison patrol missions.

The Patron's Pride is the Alliance ship tasked with returning Alliance soldiers home now that the Pandaria campaign was over. During the return voyage a storm sea at least killed one person one broad and forced another, Tarlo Mondan off board and into the sea. The captain of the the Patron's Pride decided to continue home, an act that Tarlo did not disagree with by remarking to himself that; "Better one man overboard than a hundred."
The Path of Victors is the main road in the lower area of Highmaul, leading out from the Coliseum.
Patch 6.2.3a is what Wowpedia is calling the small client patches released after patch 6.2.3.
Patch 6.2.4a is what Wowpedia is calling the small client patches released after patch 6.2.4.
The Patch of Risen Saber Pelt is a quest reward from Lieutenant of the Tower.

Patch 7.1.0: Return to Karazhan is Legion's first medium patch. It features a mythic-only dungeon that takes place in Karazhan named Return to Karazhan, the Nighthold and Trial of Valor raids, and continues the Suramar campaign with the "Insurrection" chapter. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on 14 September 2016. Its release date was announced on 14 October 2016. Last patch notes update: 2016-10-24

Patron of War was a title rewarded for linking one's Battle.Net account to their [http://www.twitch.tv Twitch] account and watching the official livestream for a certain event. The title will show after the character's name, in the following format: :, Patron of War

Patch 7.1.5 is Legion's second medium patch, updating some minor systems but not introducing any major new features. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on 15 November 2016. Its release date was announced on 6 January 2017. Last patch notes update: 2017-01-10, 12:30 p.m. PST

Patch 7.2.0: The Tomb of Sargeras is the first content patch of Legion, focusing on assaulting the Broken Shore once more and closing the portal within the Tomb of Sargeras. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on January 19, 2017. Its release date was announced on March 23, 2017 during a Live Developer Q&A with Senior Game Designer Ryan Shwayder. Last patch notes update: 2017-03-27
Pathstalker Gilen is a gnome located at the Greyfang Enclave in Dalaran.

Patient Zero is a Legion raid achievement earned from killing Helya while all raid members but one are afflicted with Fetid Rot, in Trial of Valor on Normal difficulty or higher. Fetid Rot comes from the Grimelord that spawns in phases 1 and 2. It is best for two players to bounce the debuff between each other, and then share it with the rest of the raid bar one when Helya is on low health.

Patch 7.2.5 is Legion's third medium patch, with a focus on class design and updating some features. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on April 11, 2017. Its release date was announced on June 7, 2017 during a Developer Q&A with Senior Game Designer Paul Kubit. Last patch notes update: 2017-06-13

Patch 7.3.0: Shadows of Argus is the second content patch of World of Warcraft: Legion, focusing on assaulting Argus, the Burning Legion's capital world. It was first announced during BlizzCon 2016. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on June 28, 2017. Its release date was announced on August 23, 2017 during the gamescom 2017 reveal ceremony. Last patch notes update: 2017-08-23
Patrick Dawson is a production director at Blizzard Entertainment, and former lead software engineer.

Patch 7.3.2 is a minor patch to World of Warcraft: Legion, focused around updating a few of the backend systems in addition to making some final adjustments in preparation for the release of the Antorus, the Burning Throne raid. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on September 20, 2017 and released on October 24, 2017. Last patch notes update: 2017-10-20

Patch 7.3.5 is Legion's fourth medium patch, focusing on scaling zones and player versus player changes. It was announced during BlizzCon 2017. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on November 30, 2017 and released on January 16, 2018.

Patch 8.0.1, released July 17, 2018, is the systems patch for World of Warcraft: Battle for Azeroth, introducing new systems, removing old systems, and applying another stat squish in preparation for the launch of the expansion.
The Patchwork Hut is a placable tent that provides a stat bonus if rested in.

Patrick Wyatt was the Vice President of Research and Development and the lead programmer at Blizzard Entertainment. He was the leader of Battle.net gaming network's programming and a major contributor on the multiplayer parts of StarCraft, Diablo, and Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness. He has been with Blizzard for more than eight years, including working on games like and . He left Blizzard in 2000 and founded with Mike O'Brien and Jeff Strain.

Patch 8.1.0: Tides of Vengeance is the first content patch of Battle for Azeroth, first announced in a [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v0WKnDcvSzE Developer Live Stream with Ion Hazzikostas] on September 18th, 2018. Tides of Vengeance features two new raids: Battle of Dazar'alor, an Alliance assault on Zuldazar; and the Crucible of Storms, located beneath the Shrine of the Storm. The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on September 21, 2018. Last patch notes update: 2019-01-22

Patch 9.0.5 is the first medium patch for World of Warcraft: Shadowlands. The patch is "focused on improving systems, rewards, Covenant and Legendary tuning, and bug fixes. Valor Points are now earnable in Mythic Keystone dungeons, and Valor can be used to upgrade new Mythic Keystone gear rewards. Changes to Covenants and Legendaries are intended to provide more gameplay options for crafting and utilizing Legendary items in specific situations, and to make sure that more players feel that the Covenant that suits their aesthetic, narrative, or other preferences for their character also feels more viable for their preferred playstyle." Updated March 8 – 6:00 p.m. PST

Patch 9.1.0: Chains of Domination is the first content patch of Shadowlands, announced at BlizzConline on February 19, 2021. It was pushed to the Public Test Realm on April 13, 2021 and went live in the Americas region on June 29, 2021.

The Path of Rebirth is the road that stretches from Hibernal Hollow all the way to the Grove of Awakening in the Heart of the Forest. Part of the road branches off into the Highland Path to the Gormhive Defensive Wall.

Patch 9.2.0: Eternity's End is the second content patch of Shadowlands, announced on 11 November 2021 and released on 22 February 2022. It introduces the Zereth Mortis zone, Sepulcher of the First Ones raid, and Zovaal's final chapter.
